title: The mosque of palm trunks
hook: in Medina the Prophet's Mosque is built of mud brick and palm, and he carries bricks

segments.voice: Yesterday, Quba, the first mosque, stones carried by the Prophet himself. Your line was lift a stone too.

Today in Medina, the Prophet's Mosque is vast: white marble, a forest of columns, a green dome over his grave, pilgrims from all over the world. Strip it back to the first version. A patch of ground where dates were laid out to dry. Walls of sun-dried mud brick. Tree trunks for pillars. Palm branches for a roof, which leaked when it rained. A floor of bare earth. And among the people carrying the bricks, sweating in the heat, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ himself. Today: the mosque of palm trunks.
screen: `MARBLE AND A GREEN DOME.` → `MUD, PALM, BARE EARTH.` → `HE CARRIED BRICKS.`

segments.voice: The story is in Sahih al-Bukhari. When the Prophet reached the center of Medina, the land where his camel knelt belonged to two orphan boys. They offered it to him as a gift; he insisted on paying for it. The plot had some palm trees and some old graves. The trees were cut down, and their trunks lined up as pillars. The walls went up in mud brick, and the roof was palm leaves laid over beams. The companions carried the bricks, chanting a short rhyming verse as they worked, and the Prophet carried bricks with them and chanted along. It was built plainly, and on purpose. It had to be: there was no money. But even later, when there was, the mosque stayed simple for a long time. A bare floor under a palm-leaf roof, so when it rained, people prayed in mud. A hadith even describes the Prophet rising from prostration at the dawn prayer one Ramadan with mud and water on his forehead. And one palm trunk has its own story. Before there was a pulpit, the Prophet used to lean against a trunk when he gave the Friday sermon. When a small wooden pulpit was built and he stepped up onto it, Sahih al-Bukhari says the trunk cried out, like a child, and the Prophet came down and put his hand on it until it quieted. The Prophet's Mosque began as mud, palm and earth. Everything that came later was built on that.
screen: `TWO ORPHANS' LAND, PAID FOR.` · `TRUNKS FOR PILLARS, PALM FOR A ROOF.` · `A BARE FLOOR, AND MUD.` · `THE TRUNK THAT CRIED.` · then, large: `BUILT PLAINLY.`

segments.voice: If you can, sit on the floor for this, with no cushion, or just a thin one, and feel how close you are to the ground. In that first mosque, people prayed on bare earth, shoulder to shoulder. Notice what it's like to have nothing between you and the floor but your own clothes, and let it be plain.
Prophet's Mosque. The first building in Medina: mud brick walls, palm-trunk pillars, and a roof of palm leaves.
Your line: built plainly. Mud brick, palm trunks, and a roof that leaked. Day two hundred fifty-eight, done.

howItsDone: Muslims hold the Prophet's Mosque in Medina among their holiest places, and pilgrims visit it; many local mosques are simple rooms, often with carpets on the floor and no furniture.

fork.setup: two orphan boys offer you their land for the new mosque, free. you're the leader of the whole community. what do you do?
options: insist on paying them for it.
fork.reveal: he insisted on paying the orphans. the hadith doesn't give his reason; some readers see care for orphans in it.

original.note: Arabic: the Prophet's Mosque, in Medina.

trapdoor: what you thought: a grand mosque from the start.
what it means: mud brick, palm-trunk pillars, a palm-leaf roof, an earth floor, built by everyone, the Prophet among them.
what a scholar hears: Bukhari 428 gives the build, 3583 the crying trunk (hanin al-jidh'), a story narrated by many companions.
recall: love that keeps showing itself in deeds
kindness working in ways too fine to see

chat.says: Was the Prophet's Mosque in Medina always huge and grand?
options: No: mud brick walls, palm-trunk pillars, and a leaky roof of leaves.
Yes, it was built of marble from the start, with a green dome.
It was built by two orphan boys as a gift, before he arrived.
chat.meaning: The first Prophet's Mosque had mud brick walls, palm trunks for pillars and a palm-leaf roof that leaked in the rain.

Prophet's Mosque.meaning: the mosque the Prophet built in Medina

Medina.meaning: the city the Prophet moved to from Mecca

al-Bukhari.meaning: the scholar whose hadith collection tells this story

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 428; 3906 (the land, the orphans, the building)
Sahih al-Bukhari 2016 (mud on his forehead in Ramadan)
Sahih al-Bukhari 3583, 3584 (the palm trunk that cried)

notes: The orphans are named Sahl and Suhayl in Bukhari 3906; the script leaves the names out. Bukhari 428 says the land was offered free and the Prophet bought it; confirm the retelling.
'A patch of ground where dates were laid out to dry' (a mirbad) follows the sirah; confirm.
Modern capacity of the mosque stated loosely ('many hundreds of thousands'); confirm or soften.
Bukhari 2016 places the mud on his forehead at the dawn prayer on the twenty-first of Ramadan; the script now says 'at the dawn prayer one Ramadan'. Confirm.

Editor review (2026-10-01): fixed a contradiction: the bricks were 'sun-dried' and also 'from the kiln'; cut the capacity figure, 'every country on earth', 'about head height' and 'the plainest building in town'; the pebble floor (a later detail) replaced with bare earth, which Bukhari 2016's mud supports; the myth called it 'the first mosque', which contradicts day 257 (Quba), now 'the Prophet's Mosque'; the fork reveal no longer states the Prophet's motive as fact; 'second holiest' softened.
